problem: docs/MEMORY.md listed Semantic as the one memory layer not built, and privacy.excluded_memory_topics had been owed by it since it was defined. Two real retrieval flaws sat underneath: memory_list() capped at .limit(200), making anything older than the 200th memory unreachable, and goal context was selected by exact whole-word matching on words longer than three characters, which for an inflected language never links сакам/сакаше/сакав.
change: New package aries/workspace/memory/. Utterances stay in aries_workspace_memories, verbatim, in the language spoken, layer USER; conclusions go to a new aries_workspace_conclusions with confidence, rationale, decision and stage, layer LEARNED, joined by a real foreign key through aries_workspace_conclusion_sources. store.record refuses a non-human source; store.conclude refuses any layer outside MACHINE_WRITABLE and any conclusion without a source. Zep's four timestamps plus superseded_by; forget expires, never deletes. Three-stage cascade off the voice path (debounced observe_later): gate, novelty by cosine against a cached float32 matrix, then one bare-enum local decision with a calibrated probability. Conclusion text is a COPY of the utterance, never generated, so translation is structurally impossible. Arbitration is by clock only, and a machine supersession withdraws only the LEARNED conclusion, never the USER utterance. retrieval.py gains semantic-v3 inside the existing VERSIONS scheme plus retrieval.stem for inflection, and memory_list lost its cap; learning_eval gained a named baseline so three versions no longer break its two-arm unpack. Explicit idempotent ALTER TABLE migration, tested against the installed shape.
validation: ./scripts/test.sh ALL SUITES PASSED; tests/test_memory.py adds 126 checks. Migration: 12 ADD COLUMNs on the live shape, 0 on a second pass, and the migrated shape equals the create_all shape. Measured here: embed 7.5-9.7 ms (e5-base-int8 ONNX, CPU); mat@q over 10000x768 cached float32 1.06 ms (100k rows 10.9 ms); memory scoring over the fixture 0.10 ms vs 3.69 ms lexical; stage-3 88-115 ms warm. Experiment in experiments/memory/, one command ./scripts/aries-memory-eval, 45 utterances (15 real transcriptions from the voice journal) x 25 probes x 5 variants, paired McNemar, reproduced identically four times. 25 developer-authored probes; no p-value is significant. Against the honest baseline (store everything verbatim, same embedder, stage-1 privacy gate only) extraction retrieved ONE FEWER answer, 17/23 vs 18/23, p=1.000, and was the only variant returning no stale and no refused memory, 25/25 vs 23/25, p=0.500, on 24 rows instead of 33 at 27 model calls. Recorded as a cost optimisation on retrieval, not a capability.
limitations: One of three supersessions was WRONG at confidence 1.000 and destroyed a true memory; unmitigated, because a confidence floor would not have caught it and a single-neighbour prompt measured worse. Only the layer rule bounds the damage. Escalation was 60%, far above SAGE's 16-18%, because e5's cosine for short sentences spans only 0.83-0.99. The 0.97/0.85 band is calibrated for this embedder: under bge-m3 nothing escalated, so the extraction question has been asked of one embedder only. bge-m3 changes the retrieval answer entirely, 23/23 and MRR 0.927 against e5's 18/23 and 0.659 - the embedder is worth five answers, the cascade minus one - and the default stays e5 on availability not quality, since bge-m3 needs ollama, 1.2 GB of VRAM shared with the decision model, and 38 ms per embedding; requesting it while qwen2.5:7b held the GPU wedged ollama for seven minutes and it had to be restarted. Two defects were found by building, not reasoning: the int8 embedder was not a function of its input (cosine 0.947 between the same text alone and in a batch of 45; fixed to 0 drift at 1.6x cost), and novelty compared a query-prefixed question against passage-prefixed statements, so a restatement scored 0.95 against itself.
